items.stem: Complete the statement: Limited liability means that shareholders …
options: are never liable for any company debts
are personally liable for all company debts
can lose no more than the amount they have paid or agreed to pay for their shares
items.answer: can lose no more than the amount they have paid or agreed to pay for their shares
items.markingKey: can lose no more than the amount they have paid or agreed to pay for their shares. Liability limited to share capital [1]

items.stem: Distinguish between a shareholder and a debenture holder.
items.answer: A shareholder is an owner who receives dividends at the directors' discretion and has voting rights (ordinary shares); a debenture holder is a lender who receives fixed interest, which must be paid, and is repaid before shareholders on liquidation.
items.markingKey: Owner vs lender [1]; dividend vs fixed interest/priority [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain two advantages to a sole trader of converting the business into a private limited company.
items.answer: Limited liability protects personal assets; easier to raise capital by selling shares; separate legal entity gives continuity.
items.markingKey: Two advantages explained [1 each] [2]

items.stem: Mateo bought 8,000 ordinary shares of $0.25 each in Condor Ltd, paying $0.85 per share. The company also has $280,000 of 5% debentures. This year it made a profit from operations of $70,000. Calculate the maximum amount Mateo could lose if Condor Ltd went into liquidation.
items.markingKey: 8,000 × $0.85 = $6,800.00 [1]; limited liability – no further personal liability [1] [2]

items.stem: Tomás bought 1,500 ordinary shares of $0.50 each in Lynx Ltd, paying $0.80 per share. The company also has $380,000 of 4% debentures. This year it made a profit from operations of $73,000. Calculate the maximum amount Tomás could lose if Lynx Ltd went into liquidation.

items.stem: Complete the statement: Preference shareholders usually receive …
options: a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders
interest that must be paid by law
a variable dividend after ordinary shareholders
items.answer: a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders
items.markingKey: a fixed rate of dividend before ordinary shareholders. Priority, fixed rate [1]

items.stem: Distinguish between ordinary shares and preference shares.
items.answer: Ordinary shares carry votes and a variable dividend paid after preference dividends; preference shares have a fixed dividend paid first and priority for repayment, but usually no votes.
items.markingKey: Ordinary – votes, variable, last [1]; preference – fixed, priority, no votes [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a company keeps retained earnings rather than paying them all as dividends.
items.answer: To finance growth and replacement of assets without borrowing, to keep a buffer for poor years and to maintain liquidity.
items.markingKey: Internal finance for growth [1]; buffer/liquidity [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why debenture interest is deducted in the income statement but dividends are not.
items.answer: Debenture interest is a cost of borrowing (an expense) that must be paid; dividends are distributions of profit to owners and are shown in the statement of changes in equity.
items.markingKey: Interest – expense of borrowing [1]; dividends – distribution to owners/SOCE [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a company's income statement shows a tax charge but a sole trader's does not.
items.answer: A company is a separate legal entity taxed on its profits; a sole trader's profit is taxed as the owner's personal income.
items.markingKey: Company taxed separately [1]; sole trader – personal tax [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain the purpose of the statement of changes in equity.
items.answer: It shows how each component of equity (share capital, premium, reserves, retained earnings) changed during the year: profit, dividends, share issues and transfers.
items.markingKey: Reconciles opening to closing equity [1]; examples of movements [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why directors may transfer profits to a general reserve.
items.answer: To show that profits are retained for future use (e.g. expansion or replacement) and to restrict the amount seen as available for dividends.
items.markingKey: Retain for future use [1]; signal/restrict dividends [1] [2]

items.stem: Tamarind Ltd has issued 550,000 ordinary shares of $0.25 each and $180,000 of 8% preference shares of $1 each. Profit for the year was $108,000. The directors paid the preference dividend and an ordinary dividend of 5 cents per share. The owner calculated the ordinary dividend as $6,875. Explain the error and calculate the correct ordinary dividend, showing your working.
items.answer: The dividend per share was applied to the nominal value of share capital instead of to the number of shares. Correct ordinary dividend: $27,500.
